action: Executed one bounded symbolic restart/reconstruction falsification probe. Compared epoch-only certificate fencing against current-epoch + exact-effect-identity + post-renewal-freshness fencing across unchanged-old, stale-relabelled, wrong-effect, and fresh-same-effect cases.
result: Epoch-only fencing rejects an unchanged old-epoch certificate but is insufficient if reconstruction re-labels a stale observation into the renewed epoch or accepts a certificate for the wrong effect. The composite fence rejects both hazards and still authorizes conditional replay/skip when a newly fresh decisive same-effect certificate exists. Renewal therefore creates an evidence-acquisition obligation rather than action authority.
tested_scope: Serialized single-writer durable-intent symbolic model with deterministic effect ids, immutable raw observation timestamps, explicit evidence epochs, truthful freshness, and a simulated missed-run boundary. No concurrency, target corruption, nondeterministic ids, distributed consensus, or claim of liveness without fresh decisive observation.
conflict_check: CLEAN semantic inputs only: latest instruction manifest/lifecycle, frozen sanitized root, frozen neuroscience config, and own neuroscience state/checkpoint/artifact. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role, scheduler, or protected-primary semantics were consumed.
exact_continuation: Next valid invocation: test crash consistency of evidence-epoch renewal as a single state transition. Symbolically split renewal into durable fields (epoch number, epoch_started_at, effect identity fence, last-certificate pointer) and inject one crash after each write boundary.
